transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-01-15 16:00 PST | Duration: 62m
Attendees: Claire (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya (Skyline Head of ML), Ethan (Platform), Marta (CISO), James (Product), Oliver (Finance)

[00:00] Claire: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda — intro, cost posture & perf goals, security constraints, then next steps. Priya, do you want to kick with how you guys are currently evaluating inference economics?
[00:18] Priya: Yeah, thanks. So we have a couple of features rolling to prod in Q2 — high volume doc summarization and an in-app analyst assistant. We're estimating 5–10M tokens a month initially. Main question is, can we get below our target of $0.0009 per token for generation including embeddings and rerankers combined.
[00:36] Diego: Got it. When you say per-token, is that all-in hosted API pricing or your internal marginal cost target if you self-host?
[00:45] Priya: All-in. We need a number that finance can sign off on. But we are open to a hybrid approach if it moves the needle.
[00:52] Claire: Helpful. Oliver from finance — any constraints on commit vs pay-as-you-go?
[00:57] Oliver: We have a Q1 budget band; procurement prefers a pilot on hosted, then evaluate dedicated if the economics and SLOs meet our internal thresholds. But we need clarity on how Redwood batching and caching can reduce token chargeable consumption.
[01:12] Samir: Quick note — Redwood charges per token generated/consumed at the API layer, but batching, prefix/KV cache, and shorter context can reduce billable tokens per logical request because of reuse. We can model both amortized and marginal cases.
[01:28] Ethan: Do you have numbers or an example of how batching helps? Our workload is bursty — spikes during market open and also background async jobs.
[01:38] Diego: Sure, simple example: with continuous batching and micro-batching windows we can consolidate requests that have overlapping prefixes. That reduces duplicate forward passes and reduces effective tokens billed if you can reuse cached KV states — for summarization we often see 20–40% token savings on prefix-heavy traffic in our customers' pilots.
[01:57] Priya: 20–40% is significant. But that seems optimistic — what does it assume about prompt structure and concurrency?
[02:06] Diego: Assumes moderate prompt reuse, and a batching window of ~25–50ms in a hosted setting. If you go to Dedicated, you can tune batch sizes and batching latency tolerances more aggressively because you control capacity.
[02:19] James: So Dedicated gives more control, but hosted might be simpler for our pilot. What about quantized models? Can Redwood serve int8 or Q4_0 variants to lower cost?
[02:29] Samir: Yes — our runtime supports quantized variants and kernel selection per model. Those typically reduce GPU memory and cost per token but can affect output quality. We recommend running eval sets — Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[02:43] Priya: We absolutely need quality baselines. Finance won't accept cost wins that break accuracy on key prompts.
[02:49] Claire: For the pilot we should pair cost checkpoints with prompt-level quality monitoring — we'll attach a small eval suite. Diego, can you include quality regression thresholds in the pilot plan?
[02:59] Diego: Yep. We'll propose acceptance criteria: <=10% regression on top-5 prompt metrics, latency P95 <= 600ms for interactive flows, and avg cost per logical op below target.
[03:11] Marta: On security — we run in a regulated space. SOC2 is table stakes. We also need SAML SSO, vendor KMS integration, and audit logs for all inference calls. How does Redwood handle data residency and encryption at rest?
[03:25] Claire: Redwood offers Hosted with data isolation commitments, Dedicated with reserved capacity and tighter isolation, and Private (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integration. For SOC2 we can share our attestation; for KMS we support bring-your-own-key for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[03:43] Marta: Great. Can you share sample audit log formats? We need to map to our SIEM.
[03:49] Diego: Yes — we have a sample audit log schema and an endpoint for log shipping (or we can push to S3). We'll include that in the security packet.
[03:57] Marta: Also latency visibility — we require token-level latency traces for SLO verification.
[04:02] Samir: We emit per-request traces with token-level breakdowns in the Console; you can hook that into your tracing system.
[04:09] Priya: Back to costs — can you walk through an actual calculation for the doc summarization use-case? Our prompts are ~1.5k tokens input, produce ~300 tokens output per request. 200k requests per month estimated at peak.
[04:24] Diego: Rough calc: 200k * (1.5k + 300) = 360M token ops naive. With batching and prefix caching, if the majority of docs share similar headers/prompts, we might eliminate 15–30% of input re-encoding; for long docs KV cache hits on repeated reads can push savings further. On Hosted with default batching, conservatively assume 10–20% savings; on Dedicated with tuned batching and pre-warmed KV caches you can get 25–40%.
[04:52] Oliver: So in numbers, to hit $0.0009 per token we need our blended cost (compute + infra + margin) below ~ $324k per month at 360M tokens? That math seems off, but you know what I mean — we need a model to play with.
[05:05] Claire: We'll send a spreadsheet that models three scenarios: hosted default, dedicated reserved (1yr commit), and private (VPC). It will let you plug in batch savings, quantization gains, and latency tradeoffs.
[05:14] Priya: Sounds good. How do fallbacks work if the preferred model variant is out of capacity? We need graceful degradation not to block users.
[05:23] Diego: We have smart routing and fallback policies — you can specify fallbacks to cheaper model variants or to a lower capacity region. For interactive SLOs we'll recommend local warm pools and autoscaling policies.
[05:33] James: What about peaks — market open is a 15-minute heavy spike each day. How do you guarantee throughput and control cost?
[05:41] Samir: For spikes we recommend a burst pool plus reserved baseline capacity. Dedicated allows you to reserve baseline GPU throughput and have burstable spare capacity at different pricing. Also request-level throttling and backpressure strategies help protect both latency SLOs and budget.
[05:56] Marta: Procurement will ask for SLA language around latency and uptime for Dedicated. Do you provide SLAs?
[06:03] Claire: Yes, Dedicated carries SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll share the SLA language in the contract appendix.
[06:09] Priya: For the pilot, we want to run a 3-week run: week 1 smoke + integration, week 2 performance baseline, week 3 scale/burst test. Is that enough to validate cost & quality?
[06:21] Diego: That should be sufficient for unit econ and latency baselines provided traffic in testing resembles production bursts or we can replay logs. We recommend replaying a week's worth of traffic to capture variety.
[06:31] Priya: We can provide traffic logs and a small eval prompt set.
[06:35] Claire: Perfect. Marta, any blocker for giving Redwood access to an isolated test VPC or do you prefer a hosted pilot?
[06:43] Marta: For now we prefer hosted pilot with strict data handling rules; if pilot goes well we'll move to Dedicated in customer VPC or private deployment. Must be able to purge logs and have access controls.
[06:55] Oliver: From finance — what are typical commit breakpoints for Dedicated to justify the sunk cost? At what monthly token volumes does Dedicated win over hosted?
[07:04] Samir: It really depends on batchability and latency tolerances. As a rule-of-thumb, if you have steady sustained throughput above ~200–400M tokens/month and can tolerate canary-based rollouts, Dedicated often becomes cost-advantageous — but we'll give you the exact cross-over in the spreadsheet with your numbers.
[07:20] Ethan: One technical question — does Redwood expose KV cache hit rates and per-token billing reconciliation? We need to reconcile invoices to telemetry.
[07:28] Diego: Yes — Console exposes token-level billing breakdowns and cache/batch hit metrics; we also provide reconciliation reports you can tie to your telemetry.
[07:36] Priya: Regarding model variants, can we pin a version and do A/B rollouts? We want to test quantized vs fp16 for quality.
[07:44] Claire: You can pin model versions, do canary rollouts and A/B tests, and set automatic fallback policies if quality/regression metrics cross thresholds. We'll propose a rollout plan.
[07:55] James: On the security doc — will Redwood accept an NDA or do you need procurement paperwork?
[08:02] Claire: We can sign an NDA; procurement paperwork and SOC2 docs can follow. We'll also send a security packet with sample audit logs, KMS options, and SSO integration notes.
[08:12] Priya: For the pilot, what are the integration touchpoints? API keys? VPC peering?
[08:18] Diego: For a hosted pilot it's API keys + per-route RBAC + limited retention options. For Dedicated or Private we'll do VPC peering or private link and KMS integration.
[08:27] Marta: About data residency — some datasets must stay in EU. Do you have region controls for hosting?
[08:33] Claire: Yes, we can host in EU regions; Dedicated/Private gives you more control over strict residency.
[08:38] Oliver: Curious if Redwood offers cost smoothing or committed discounts for seasonal spikes?
[08:44] Samir: We offer reserved capacity and monthly commit bands. For spikes we can structure burst credits or a blended rate for the first X tokens beyond committed baseline. We'll include options in the commercial proposal.
[08:55] Priya: One last thing — do you have customers with similar workloads (finance, summarization) we can reference?
[09:01] Claire: Yes — high level references available; we'll share anonymized case studies and a short note on outcomes (cost savings and latency improvements).
[09:08] James: Great. Can we also see a sample prompt-level quality dashboard?
[09:12] Samir: We'll include a screenshot and a small demo during the technical deep dive.
[09:17] Claire: Alright let's list concrete next steps...
[09:21] (brief cross talk as attendees note items)
[09:28] Priya: Also can Diego scope the latency tests — we want P50, P95, and tail latencies under both hosted and dedicated configs.
[09:36] Diego: Yes — we'll propose a benchmark plan with synthetic and replay tests.
[09:40] Claire: Cool. Anything else from Skyline?
[09:44] Marta: No, just ensure the security packet includes KMS BYOK details and audit log schemas.
[09:49] Oliver: Finance will look at the spreadsheet and follow up on pricing.
[09:53] Claire: We'll send the spreadsheet and schedule the deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[09:57] Priya: Thanks, bye.
